findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The continued-turn fail-closed branch sets Decision to (r.Kind == KindStillPresent), but the test only exercises the adjudicate kind, so mutating the still-present direction would pass every test. A regression flipping a continued still-present turn's fail-closed direction would go unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] A continued-past-verdict turn is retried up to MaxAttempts with full backoff, although a hook that fires once will likely fire on every retry. Bounded extra cost (MaxAttempts codex sessions) before failing closed; not a correctness bug.

[ADVISORY] continuedPastVerdict treats any earlier complete verdict as an interruption, including a judge that legitimately restates its verdict. Such a turn fails closed after MaxAttempts instead of recording the valid verdict; no evidence the prompts produce this.

[ADVISORY] Hook/plugin isolation and the continued-past-verdict guard were added only to the codex arm; the claude CLI judge still loads user settings (--setting-sources user), so user Stop hooks can still run in a claude/* judge. A claude/* judge could still record a hook notice as reasoning; only the empty-reasoning rule applies there.
[ADVISORY] features.hooks / features.plugins key names are assumed; a codex build with different names silently ignores them. Only the structural guard would then protect the judge.
